answer: I'd like to talk about my first day at the education consultancy where I still work. A time I felt intensely nervous was on my first day at a new job, walking into an office full of complete strangers. It was only a few months after I had finished my BBA, and it was my first proper full-time job. I had really wanted the role, which somehow made me even more [[apprehensive]] about making a bad impression. The night before, I barely slept, and I think I ironed my shirt at least twice. I even left home forty minutes early, just in case the rickshaw got stuck in traffic. My mind was racing with worries about whether I would fit in or make some embarrassing mistake. I remember my hands were slightly shaking as I introduced myself. To my relief, my new colleagues were warm and [[welcoming]], which gradually [[put me at ease]]. One senior colleague took me out for tea and explained how everything worked, which made a huge difference. By lunchtime, most of my nerves had [[melted away]], and I began to feel genuinely [[optimistic]] about the job. Looking back, I realise that my anxiety had been almost entirely in my head. What I learned was that nervousness before something important is completely natural, and it usually fades once you actually begin. That experience taught me to trust that things generally turn out far better than my worried mind predicts. When I got home that evening, my family were waiting to hear every detail over dinner.

followUps.q: Do you still feel nervous at work sometimes?
followUps.answer: Occasionally, mostly before meeting parents who are very worried about sending their child abroad. But it is a useful kind of nervousness now, because it makes me prepare properly.

followUps.q: What do you usually do to calm your nerves?
followUps.answer: I take a few slow breaths and remind myself that I have prepared. If I have time, a short walk and a cup of tea usually help me feel settled again.

note: Made it his first day at the consultancy after his BBA; added night-before and senior colleague details; plain mark 'natural' replaced by 'put me at ease' and 'melted away'.
